# Step 1: Hazard type 

This section classifies climate-related hazards mentioned in the `ElementText` column of the `adaptdata` dataset using regex-based keyword matching, aligned with the protocol’s definitions.


1. **Column Creation**  
   A new column `HazardType` is added to store the hazard category for each entry. This column is positioned after `ElementText`.

2. **Keyword Mapping**  
   Hazard categories are mapped to regex patterns that represent keywords found in the protocol definitions. These keywords are matched case-insensitively within the `ElementText`.

3. **Tagging**  
   The script loops over all hazard patterns and tags any matching rows accordingly.

---

### Hazard Categories and Associated Keywords

```{r,echo=FALSE}
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

hazard_keywords <- tribble(
  ~"Hazard Category", ~"Keywords Used",
  
  "Extreme temperature", "heat wave, heatwave, excessive heat, high temperature, extreme temperature, extreme heat, extremely low, cold waves, cold wave, snow, ice, frost, freeze, severe winter, maximum and minimum, warmer, higher occurrence of hot, glacier, snowfall, evapo, extreme weather, heat stress, hot days, hot nights",
  
  "Storm", "storm, tropical storm, cyclone, cyclones, Cyclonic activity, typhoon, typhoons, hail, lightning, thunderstorm, heavy rain, windstorm, sand storm, dust storm, tornado, violent rains, torrential, strong winds",
  
  "Drought", "drought, drought cycle, prolonged droughts, drougths, dry spell, dry days, aridity",
  
  "Wildfire", "wildfire, wild fire, forest fire, land fire, bush fire, pasture fire, fire",
  
  "Landslide", "landslide, land slide",
  
  "Flood", "flood, coastal flood, riverine flood, flash flood, ice jam flood, inundation",
  
  "Change in temperature", "change in temperature, alteration in average temperature, temperature change, temperature rise, temperature drop, consistent change in temperature, rise in temperature, increase in temperature, increases in temperature, temperature increase, increasing temperature, increased temperature, increase temperatures, higher temperatures, average temperature, annual temperature, annual mean temperature, annual air temperature, minimum temperatures, maximum temperatures, number of warm days, rising temperatures, warming temperatures",
  
  "Change in precipitation", "change in precipitation, alteration in precipitation, precipitation patterns, shift in timing, shift in amount, shift in intensity, shift in frequency, rainfall, precipitation, distribution of rains, disruption of rains, fluctuation of rains, shorter rain, earlier and ending later",
  
  "Salinization", "salinization, salt content, saltwater, salt water, salinity, increase in salt content",
  
  "Land degradation", "land degradation, decline in land quality, decline in land health, pasture degradation, desertification, loss of organic matter, degradation of land, erosion, soil erosion",
  
  "Sea level rise", "sea level rise, sea level, increase in sea level, coastal flooding, coastal erosion, beach loss, coastline retreat, submersion, water mass",
  
  "Sea temperature", "sea temperature, sea surface temperature, change in sea temperature, ocean temperature, water temperature, surface temperature, seawater surface",
  
  "Ocean acidification", "ocean acidification, reduction in pH, acidity, acidification, acidic, coral",
  
  "Pest and disease", "pest, disease, epidemic, infestation, invasion, insect infestation, vector-borne, biological event, invasive species"
)

kable(hazard_keywords, "html", escape = FALSE) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive")) %>%
  column_spec(2, width = "50em")

```

```{r,echo=FALSE}
# 1) Initialize HazardType and relocate
adaptdata$HazardType <- ""
adaptdata <- adaptdata %>% relocate(HazardType, .after = ElementText)

# 2) Define your hazard → regex map
haz_patterns <- list(
  "Extreme temperature" = paste(
    "heat wave", "heatwave", "excessive heat", "high temperature", "extreme temperature",
    "extreme heat", "extremely low", "cold waves", "cold wave", "snow", "ice", "frost",
    "freeze", "severe winter", "maximum and minimum", "warmer", "higher occurrence of hot",
    "glacier", "snowfall", "evapo","extreme weather","heat stress","hot days","hot nights", sep = "|"
  ),
  
  "Storm" = paste(
    "storm", "tropical storm", "cyclone", "cyclones","Cyclonic activity","typhoon", "typhoons", "hail",
    "lightning", "thunderstorm", "heavy rain", "windstorm", "sand storm", "dust storm",
    "tornado", "violent rains","torrential","strong winds", sep = "|"
  ),
  
  "Drought" = paste(
    "drought", "drought cycle", "prolonged droughts","drougths","dry spell","dry days","aridity", sep = "|"
  ),
  
  "Wildfire" = paste(
    "wildfire", "wild fire", "forest fire", "land fire", "bush fire", "pasture fire","fire",
    sep = "|"
  ),
  
  "Landslide" = paste(
    "landslide", "land slide", sep = "|"
  ),
  
  "Flood" = paste(
    "\\bflood(s|ing)?\\b", "coastal flood", "riverine flood", "flash flood", "ice jam flood",
    "inundation", sep = "|"
  ),
  
  "Change in temperature" = paste(
    "change in temperature", "alteration in average temperature", "temperature change",
    "temperature rise", "temperature drop", "consistent change in temperature",
    "rise in temperature", "increase in temperature", "increases in temperature",
    "temperature increase", "increasing temperature", "increased temperature",
    "increase temperatures", "higher temperatures", "average temperature",
    "annual temperature","annual mean temperature","annual air temperature","minimum temperatures","maximum temperatures","number of warm days","rising temperatures","warming temperatures", sep = "|"
  ),
  
  "Change in precipitation" = paste(
    "change in precipitation", "alteration in precipitation", "precipitation patterns",
    "shift in timing", "shift in amount", "shift in intensity", "shift in frequency",
    "rainfall", "precipitation", "distribution of rains", "disruption of rains",
    "fluctuation of rains", "shorter rain", "earlier and ending later", sep = "|"
  ),
  
  "Salinization" = paste(
    "salinization", "salt content", "saltwater", "salt water", "salinity",
    "increase in salt content", sep = "|"
  ),
  
  "Land degradation" = paste(
    "land degradation", "decline in land quality", "decline in land health",
    "pasture degradation", "desertification", "loss of organic matter",
    "degradation of land", "erosion", "soil erosion", sep = "|"
  ),
  
  "Sea level rise" = paste(
    "sea[ -]?level rise", "sea level", "increase in sea level", "coastal flooding",
    "coastal erosion", "beach loss", "coastline retreat", "submersion","water mass","sea level rise", sep = "|"
  ),
  
  "Sea temperature" = paste(
    "sea temperature", "sea surface temperature", "change in sea temperature",
    "ocean temperature", "water temperature","surface temperature","seawater surface", sep = "|"
  ),
  
  "Ocean acidification" = paste(
    "ocean acidification", "reduction in pH", "acidity", "acidification", "acidic",
    "coral", sep = "|"
  ),
  
  "Pest and disease" = paste(
    "pest", "disease", "epidemic", "infestation", "invasion", "insect infestation",
    "vector-borne", "biological event,invasive species", sep = "|"
  )
)


# 3) Safe text (no NAs)
safe_text <- ifelse(is.na(adaptdata$ElementText), "", adaptdata$ElementText)

# 4) Minimal loop to append multiple types
for(type in names(haz_patterns)) {
  # find rows that are Hazard and match the pattern
  hits <- grepl(haz_patterns[[type]], safe_text, ignore.case = TRUE)
  idx  <- which(!is.na(adaptdata$Element) & adaptdata$Element == "Hazard" & hits)
  
  if (length(idx) > 0) {
    current <- adaptdata$HazardType[idx]
    adaptdata$HazardType[idx] <- ifelse(
      current == "",
      type,
      paste(current, type, sep = ";")
    )
  }
}

# Now any Hazard row matching multiple patterns will contain e.g. "Flood;Storm;Drought"

```

## Coverage of hazard type 

```{r,echo=FALSE}
# Count number of 'Hazard' elements that received a HazardType
assigned_hazards <- adaptdata %>%
  filter(Element == "Hazard" & HazardType != "") %>%
  nrow()

# Total number of Hazard elements
total_hazards <- adaptdata %>%
  filter(Element == "Hazard") %>%
  nrow()

# Display the result
cat("Hazard rows assigned a category:", assigned_hazards, "out of", total_hazards, "\n")
cat("**Coverage Rate:**", round(assigned_hazards / total_hazards * 100, 1), "%\n")
```

## Hazard type summary data 

```{r,echo=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(DT)

# 1. Filter for hazard elements with at least one category
hazard_counts <- adaptdata %>%
  filter(Element == "Hazard" & HazardType != "") %>%
  separate_rows(HazardType, sep = ";") %>%
  count(HazardType, sort = TRUE) %>%
  rename(`Hazard Category` = HazardType, `Occurrences` = n)

# 2. Display with DT for interactivity
DT::datatable(
  hazard_counts,
  rownames = FALSE,
  options = list(
    pageLength = 10,
    autoWidth = TRUE,
    dom = 'tip'
  )
)

write.csv(hazard_counts,   "hazard_counts.csv", row.names = FALSE)

#3. Visualize hazard count


hazard_plot <- ggplot(hazard_counts,
       aes(x = reorder(`Hazard Category`, Occurrences),
           y = Occurrences,
           fill = Occurrences)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "plasma", direction = -1, guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Hazard categories by count", x = NULL, y = "Occurrences") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14)
  )

hazard_plot



```

# Step 2: Systems at risk

We assign a SystemType to each row of adaptdata where the element is "System at risk". This classification is based on the official reporting protocol definitions, which describe different climate-sensitive systems affected by hazards (e.g., agriculture, biodiversity, infrastructure).

To do this, we use a dictionary of keyword patterns that match text found in the ElementText column. These keywords are derived from the protocol and expanded where needed to capture variations in language.

Only rows where the element is "System at risk" are considered.

The following table summarizes the system categories used for classification and the corresponding keyword patterns:

```{r,echo=FALSE}
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(tibble)

system_table <- tribble(
  ~`System Type`, ~`Keywords Used`,

  "Crop", "crop, cropping systems, crop production, yield, cultivated area, agriculture, agricultural, agricultural production, agricultural pests, pest, irrigated, rain-fed, farming, land use planning, crop loss, agroecological zone, production",

  "Livestock", "livestock, pasture, pastoralist, pastoral area, grazing, animal health, productivity losses, herder, livestock loss",

  "Fisheries and aquaculture", "fish, fisheries, aquaculture, fishing, marine harvest",

  "Forest", "forest, forestry, forest product, tree, non-timber",

  "Terrestrial", "terrestrial ecosystem, terrestrial, drylands, land resource, natural resource, ecosystem structure, ecosystem services, ecological system, desertification, land degradation, soil degradation, soil erosion, environment",

  "Freshwater", "freshwater, wetlands, inland wetlands, water resource, drinking water, potable water, water quality, water availability, water supply, river, water scarcity, water shortage, hydrological cycle, water stress, water table, water source, groundwater, water supplied, dams, eutrophication, algal bloom",

  "Biodiversity", "biodiversity, flora, fauna, species, species extinction, extinction, range of species, ecosystem change",

  "Coastal", "coast, coastal, marine, mangrove, ocean, coral, beach, coastal erosion, sea level rise, blue carbon, coastal ecosystem, coastal zone",

  "Food and nutrition", "food security, food insecure, food insecurity, nutrition, malnutrition, hunger, food safety, food availability, famine, undernutrition, overnutrition, obesity",

  "Gender and inclusion", "gender, women, youth, children, elderly, inclusion, social exclusion, vulnerable group, vulnerable population, minority group, indigenous, small-scale producer, pastoralist, fishing communities, forest-based communities, high-risk regions",

  "Livelihoods and poverty", "livelihood, poverty, income, employment, labor, economic activity, loss of income, loss of livelihood, safety net, insurance, socio-economic development, tourism, subsistence, workforce, economic, tourists, outdoor activities, ski, vacation",

  "Health", "health, mental health, morbidity, mortality, vector-borne disease, water-borne disease, infectious disease, respiratory disease, malaria, epidemic, climate-sensitive disease, heat morbidity, disease, deaths, human lives, pollution, life expectancy",

  "Infrastructure and services", "infrastructure, critical infrastructure, services, critical services, road, bridge, electricity, power supply, energy, water supply, sanitation, hygiene, education, school, building, housing, settlement, evacuation, telecom, transport, waste management, power, hydropower, railways, port, industry, material, industries",

  "Human security and Peace", "migration, displacement, conflict, armed conflict, national security, human security, organized conflict, climate-induced migration, refugee, peace"
)

kable(system_table, "html", escape = FALSE, align = "l") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  column_spec(2, width = "50em", extra_css = "word-wrap: break-word; white-space: normal;")

```

```{r,echo=FALSE}
# 1) Initialize SystemType and relocate
adaptdata$SystemType <- ""
adaptdata <- adaptdata %>% relocate(SystemType, .after = HazardType)

# 2) Define your system‐to‐pattern map
sys_patterns <- list(
  Crop = paste(
    "crop", "cropping systems", "crop production", "yield", "cultivated area",
    "agriculture", "agricultural", "agricultural production", "agricultural pests",
    "pest", "irrigated", "rain-fed", "farming", "land use planning", "crop loss","agroecological zone","production", sep = "|"
  ),
  
  Livestock = paste(
    "livestock", "pasture", "pastoralist", "pastoral area", "grazing", 
    "animal health", "productivity losses", "herder", "livestock loss", sep = "|"
  ),
  
  `Fisheries and aquaculture` = paste(
    "fish", "fisheries", "aquaculture", "fishing", "marine harvest", sep = "|"
  ),
  
  Forest = paste(
    "forest", "forestry", "forest product", "tree", "non-timber", sep = "|"
  ),
  
  Terrestrial = paste(
    "terrestrial ecosystem", "terrestrial", "drylands", "land resource", 
    "natural resource", "ecosystem structure", "ecosystem services",
    "ecological system", "desertification", "land degradation", 
    "soil degradation", "soil erosion", "environment", sep = "|"
  ),
  
  Freshwater = paste(
    "freshwater", "wetlands", "inland wetlands", "water resource", "drinking water",
    "potable water", "water quality", "water availability", "water supply",
    "river", "water scarcity", "water shortage", "hydrological cycle",
    "water stress", "water table", "water source", "groundwater","water supplied","dams","eutrophication","algal bloom", sep = "|"
  ),
  
  Biodiversity = paste(
    "biodiversity", "flora", "fauna", "species", "species extinction",
    "extinction", "range of species", "ecosystem change", sep = "|"
  ),
  
  Coastal = paste(
    "coast", "coastal", "marine", "mangrove", "ocean", "coral", 
    "beach", "coastal erosion", "sea level rise", "blue carbon", 
    "coastal ecosystem", "coastal zone", sep = "|"
  ),
  
  `Food and nutrition` = paste(
    "food security", "food insecure", "food insecurity", "nutrition", 
    "malnutrition", "hunger", "food safety", "food availability", 
    "famine", "undernutrition", "overnutrition", "obesity", sep = "|"
  ),
  
  `Gender and inclusion` = paste(
    "gender", "women", "youth", "children", "elderly", "inclusion",
    "social exclusion", "vulnerable group", "vulnerable population",
    "minority group", "indigenous", "small-scale producer", 
    "pastoralist", "fishing communities", "forest-based communities",
    "high-risk regions", sep = "|"
  ),
  
  `Livelihoods and poverty` = paste(
    "livelihood", "poverty", "income", "employment","labor", "economic activity",
    "loss of income", "loss of livelihood", "safety net","insurance", 
    "socio-economic development", "tourism", "subsistence", "workforce","economic","tourism","tourists","outdoor activities","ski","vacation",
    sep = "|"
  ),
  
  Health = paste(
    "health", "mental health", "morbidity", "mortality", "vector-borne disease",
    "water-borne disease", "infectious disease", "respiratory disease", 
    "malaria", "epidemic", "climate-sensitive disease", "heat morbidity","disease","deaths","human lives","pollution","life expectancy", sep = "|"
  ),
  
  `Infrastructure and services` = paste(
    "infrastructure", "critical infrastructure", "services", "critical services",
    "road", "bridge", "electricity", "power supply", "energy", 
    "water supply", "sanitation", "hygiene", "education", "school", 
    "building", "housing", "settlement", "evacuation", "telecom", 
    "transport", "waste management","power","hydropower","railways","port","industry","material","industries", sep = "|"
  ),
  
  `Human security and Peace` = paste(
    "migration", "displacement", "conflict", "armed conflict", 
    "national security", "human security", "organized conflict", 
    "climate-induced migration", "refugee", "peace", sep = "|"
  )
)


# 3) Build a safe text vector (no NAs)
safe_text <- ifelse(is.na(adaptdata$ElementText), "", adaptdata$ElementText)

# 4) Loop through patterns, appending multiple matches with ";"
for(type in names(sys_patterns)) {
  # identify rows to tag
  idx <- which(
    adaptdata$Element == "System at risk" &
    grepl(sys_patterns[[type]], safe_text, ignore.case = TRUE)
  )
  
  if(length(idx)) {
    current <- adaptdata$SystemType[idx]
    adaptdata$SystemType[idx] <- ifelse(
      current == "",
      type,
      paste(current, type, sep = ";")
    )
  }
}

# Now any "System at risk" row matching multiple patterns will have
# e.g. "Crop;Livestock;Food and nutrition" in SystemType.

```

## Coverage of system at risk type 

```{r,echo=FALSE}
# Compute number of System at risk rows
total_system_rows <- sum(adaptdata$Element == "System at risk", na.rm = TRUE)

# Count how many received a classification
assigned_system_rows <- sum(adaptdata$Element == "System at risk" & adaptdata$SystemType != "", na.rm = TRUE)

# Print basic coverage stats
cat("**System at Risk Coverage:**", assigned_system_rows, "of", total_system_rows, 
    "rows were successfully assigned a category.\n")
cat("**Coverage Rate:**", round(assigned_system_rows / total_system_rows * 100, 1), "%\n")

```

```{r,echo=FALSE}
# --- 1. Add Region from overview ---
region_key <- overview %>%
  select(Country, Region) %>%
  distinct()

# add manual fixes for missing countries
manual_add <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Country,        ~Region,
  "Moldova",       "Eastern Europe",
  "Phillipines",   "Asia-Pacific",
  "Russia",        "Eastern Europe",
  "Türkiye",       "Asia-Pacific",
  "USA",           "Western Europe and Other states"
)

# combine with existing region_key
region_key <- region_key %>%
  bind_rows(manual_add) %>%
  distinct()


adaptdata_with_region <- adaptdata %>%
  left_join(region_key, by = "Country")

# --- 2. Filter + separate multiple SystemType values ---
system_counts <- adaptdata_with_region %>%
  filter(Element == "System at risk" & !is.na(SystemType) & SystemType != "") %>%
  separate_rows(SystemType, sep = ";") %>%
  count(Region, SystemType, sort = TRUE) %>%

# --- 3. Table ---

  rownames = FALSE,
  options = list(pageLength = 10, autoWidth = TRUE, dom = 'tip'),

)

# --- 4a. Facetted by region ---
system_plot<-ggplot(system_counts,
       aes(x = reorder(`System at Risk Category`, Occurrences),
           y = Occurrences,
           fill = Region)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  coord_flip() +
```

# Step 3: Sectors
We classify sectors in two ways:

1. **SectorType (IPCC categories)** — based on keywords found in the `Sector` and `SystemType` columns. This follows the sector taxonomy defined in the MPGs (Table 1).
2. **SectorType_GGA (GGA themes)** — which maps the sectors into broader Global Goal on Adaptation (GGA) thematic groups as per the protocol.

The tagging logic first applies regular expressions to the text in `Sector`, with some fallback rules based on the `SystemType` when relevant. The classification is additive and accounts for overlapping sector concepts.

Below is a summary table of sector categories and the associated keywords used.


### SectorType (IPCC categories) - Keywords used

```{r,echo=FALSE}


# Patterns per protocol + your extra phrases/stems
ipcc_patterns <- list(
  "Food, fiber and other ecosystem products" =
    paste0(
      "(",
      paste(c(
        # protocol terms
        "agri","agro","agriculture","food","crop","livestock","animal","fish",
        "fisheries","aquacultur","aquaculture","seed","irrigation","value chain",
        "land use","land tenure","land and forestry","agroforest",
        # extras seen in your prior rules
        "Agriculture,? (?:forest|and other land uses)","land affairs","land reforms",
        "Food and nutrition","Crop","Livestock","Fisheries and aquaculture",
        "Agriculture and food security","Agriculture, Climate services, Others",
        "Sustainable development, Agriculture"
      ), collapse="|"),
      ")"
    ),

  "Terrestrial and freshwater ecosystems" =
    paste0(
      "(",
      paste(c(
        # protocol terms
        "forest","environ","environment","ecosystem","biodiversity","natural","ecolog",
        "wildlife","REDD","peatland","protected area",
        # extras (including misspelling & broad terms you used)
        "enviornment","Terrestrial","Freshwater","Biodiversity","land\\b"
      ), collapse="|"),
      ")"
    ),

  "Ocean and coastal ecosystems" =
    paste0(
      "(",
      paste(c(
        # protocol terms
        "ocean","marine","coast","coastal","coastal land use","coastal zone","blue carbon","mangrove",
        # extras
        "Tourism and Coastal Zone Management","Coastal zone management"
      ), collapse="|"),
      ")"
    ),

  "Water, sanitation and hygiene" =
    paste0(
      "(",
      paste(c(
        # protocol terms
        "sanitation","water and sanitation","sewerage","hygiene",
        # extras
        "water security","water use","water and energy","water, sanitation and waste"
      ), collapse="|"),
      ")"
    ),

  "Cities, settlements and key infrastructure" =
    paste0(
      "(",
      paste(c(
        # protocol terms
        "city","cities","urban","settlement","infrastructure","housing","habitat",
        "industr","waste","transport","energy",
        # extras (phrases & sectors you mapped before)
        "Infrastructure, transport and building","Infrastructure and services",
        "landfills","sanitary landfills","mining","mineral resources","mineral products",
        "telecommunications","Telecommunications",
        "Cities and Built Environment","Land Use and Human Settlements Development",
        "Habitat, urban planning and development of the territory",
        "Housing, Territorial Development and Urban Planning",
        "Renewable Energy","Urban planning and infrastructure",
        "Urban Development & Tourism","Private sector/trade; Manufacturing; Business process"
      ), collapse="|"),
      ")"
    ),

  "Health, wellbeing and communities" =
    paste0(
      "(",
      paste(c(
        # protocol terms
        "health","well-?being","wellbeing","nutrition","culture",
        "territorial communit","local knowledge",
        # extras you used/mapped
        "territorial communities","Human security","Vulnerable communities","Territorial development"
      ), collapse="|"),
      ")"
    ),

  "Livelihoods, poverty and sustainable development" =
    paste0(
      "(",
      paste(c(
        # protocol terms
        "social","poverty","people","econom","capacity","education","employment",
        "tourism","rural development","sustainable development","economic and social infrastructure",
        # extras
        "Livelihoods and poverty","protection","social protection","transfer",
        "income","revenue","social infrastructures",
        "Education, research","Education, training, research",
        "Multiple: Social Economy, Tourism","Multiple: Social Affairs, Women and Family",
        "Multiple: Planning, Rural development","Multiple: Sustainable development, Planning"
      ), collapse="|"),
      ")"
    ),

  "Crosscutting" =
    paste0(
      "(",
      paste(c(
        # protocol terms
        "cross[- ]?cutting","cross[- ]?sectoral","innovation","research","R&D","integration",
        "empower","gender","women","youth","disaster","risk","climate( service)?",
        "meteo","warning","governance","legislation","polic(?:y|ies)","institution","M&E",
        # extras
        "devolution","private sector","public sector","territory","spatial planning","\\bplanning\\b"
      ), collapse="|"),
      ")"
    )
)

# Tie-break priority = list order above (adjust if you want a different precedence)
ipcc_priority <- names(ipcc_patterns)

# Ensure the column exists and sits after Sector
if (!"SectorType" %in% names(adaptdata)) adaptdata$SectorType <- NA_character_
adaptdata <- adaptdata %>% relocate(SectorType, .after = Sector)

# Build the text to scan (Sector first, with SystemType as context/fallback)
adaptdata <- adaptdata %>%
  mutate(
    .ipcc_text = paste0(
      coalesce(as.character(Sector), ""), " ",
      coalesce(as.character(SystemType), "")
    )
  ) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    # count matches per sector
    .counts = list(vapply(ipcc_patterns, function(pat) {
      str_count(.ipcc_text, regex(pat, ignore_case = TRUE))
    }, integer(1))),
    # pick a single best sector; NA if no matches
    SectorType = {
      counts <- unlist(.counts)
      if (all(counts == 0L)) NA_character_ else {
        winners <- which(counts == max(counts))
        ipcc_priority[winners[1]]
      }
    }
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-.ipcc_text, -.counts)

```

## sector for all rows

```{r}
# Ensure column exists
if (!"SectorType_GGA" %in% names(adaptdata)) adaptdata$SectorType_GGA <- NA_character_

adaptdata <- adaptdata %>%
  mutate(
    # Use Sector if available; if not, fall back to ElementText
    .gga_text = if_else(
      !is.na(Sector) & str_trim(Sector) != "",
      paste0(as.character(Sector), " ", coalesce(as.character(ElementText), "")),
      coalesce(as.character(ElementText), "")
    )
  ) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    .counts_gga = list(vapply(gga_patterns, function(pat) {
      str_count(.gga_text, regex(pat, ignore_case = TRUE))
    }, integer(1))),
    SectorType_GGA = {
      # Special case: Sector exactly "water"
      if (!is.na(Sector) && str_to_lower(str_trim(Sector)) == "water") {
        "Water and sanitation"
      } else {
        cnt <- unlist(.counts_gga)
        if (all(cnt == 0L)) NA_character_ else {
          winners <- which(cnt == max(cnt))
          gga_priority[winners[1]]
        }
      }
    }
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-.gga_text, -.counts_gga)
```

```{r,echo=FALSE}

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
library(stringr)

adaptdata <- read.csv("data/adaptdata_results_nano6.csv")

region_key <- overview %>%
  select(Country, Region) %>%
  distinct()

manual_add <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Country,      ~Region,
  "Moldova",     "Eastern Europe",
  "Phillipines", "Asia-Pacific",
  "Russia",      "Eastern Europe",
  "Türkiye",     "Asia-Pacific",
  "USA",         "Western Europe and Other states"
)

region_key <- region_key %>%
  bind_rows(manual_add) %>%
  distinct()

adaptdata_with_region <- adaptdata %>%
  left_join(region_key, by = "Country")

# --- Fixed order (renamed NA-like -> "Not specific to a theme") ---
theme_order <- c(
  "Water and sanitation",
  "Food and agriculture",
  "Health",
  "Biodiversity and ecosystems",
  "Infrastructure and human settlements",
  "Poverty eradication and livelihoods",
  "Cultural heritage",
  "Not specific to a theme"
)

# --- Counts per Theme x Region ---
theme_counts_by_region <- adaptdata_with_region %>%
  filter(Element != "NA") %>%
  mutate(
    SectorType_GGA = dplyr::case_when(
      is.na(SectorType_GGA) ~ "Not specific to a theme",
      trimws(SectorType_GGA) %in% c("NA", "N/A") ~ "Not specific to a theme",
      TRUE ~ SectorType_GGA
    ),
    SectorType_GGA = factor(SectorType_GGA, levels = theme_order, ordered = TRUE),
    Region = if_else(is.na(Region) | Region == "", "Unknown", Region)
  ) %>%
  count(SectorType_GGA, Region, name = "n")

# --- Inside-stack labels (same logic as before) ---
theme_counts_by_region_lbl <- theme_counts_by_region %>%
  group_by(SectorType_GGA) %>%
  mutate(
    pct   = n / sum(n),
    label = if_else(pct >= 0.06, scales::percent(pct, accuracy = 1), "")
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

labels_df <- theme_counts_by_region_lbl %>%
  group_by(SectorType_GGA) %>%
  mutate(pct_calc = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    label2 = dplyr::case_when(
      SectorType_GGA == "Cultural heritage" ~ "",  # hide
      SectorType_GGA == "Not specific to a theme" ~ scales::percent(pct_calc, accuracy = 1), # always show
      TRUE ~ label
    ),
    label_size = if_else(
      SectorType_GGA %in% c("Health", "Poverty eradication and livelihoods"),
      2, 3
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(label2 != "")

# --- Top-of-bar % of TOTAL (right-axis ties to this) ---
bar_tops <- theme_counts_by_region %>%
  group_by(SectorType_GGA) %>%
  summarise(total_n = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(pct_total = total_n / sum(total_n),
         top_label = percent(pct_total, accuracy = 1))

total_all <- sum(bar_tops$total_n)

# --- Plot ---
ggplot(theme_counts_by_region_lbl,
       aes(x = SectorType_GGA, y = n, fill = Region)) +
  geom_col() +
  # inside-the-stack labels
  geom_text(
    data = labels_df,
    aes(label = label2, size = label_size),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5)
  ) +
  scale_size_identity(guide = "none") +
  # top-of-bar % of total
  geom_text(
    data = bar_tops,
    aes(x = SectorType_GGA, y = total_n, label = top_label),
    vjust = -0.3, fontface = "bold", size = 3.2, inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "plasma", name = "Region") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Number of data points",
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / total_all,
                        labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                        name = "Share of all extracted information"),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.12)) # headroom for top labels
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Themes covered across all Elements by Region",
    x = "Theme",
    fill = "Region"
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = function(x) stringr::str_wrap(x, width = 15)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.key.size = unit(0.8, "lines"),
    plot.margin = margin(5.5, 12, 5.5, 5.5)
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE))


```

```{r}
datatable(theme_counts_country_all,
```

# Step 4 : Climate Impact

## 4.1 GPT Extraction — impact keywords

- Each *Climate impact* passage is reduced by GPT to **short exact phrases** of consequences  
  (e.g., *“water scarcity”; “crop yield loss”; “heat-related illness”*).  
- Hazards (*“storm”*) and actions (*“irrigation”*) are excluded unless phrased as impacts  
  (e.g., *“increased flooding”*).

## 4.2 Categorization — from phrases to classes

- Phrases are mapped to a fixed set of **impact categories**  
    - Water availability shortfall  
    - Water quality deterioration  
    - Crop production loss  
    - Livestock impacts  
    - Soil degradation
    - Fisheries & aquaculture decline  
    - Food security & nutrition decline  
    - Human health burden  
    - Mental health impacts  
    - Healthcare system strain  
    - Mortality & injury  
    - Displacement & migration  
    - Damage to buildings & infrastructure  
    - Energy system impacts  
    - Transport disruption  
    - Supply chain & logistics disruptions  
    - Economic & livelihood losses  
    - Tourism & recreation impacts  
    - Ecosystem degradation & biodiversity loss  
    - Soil erosion & land degradation  
    - Marine ecosystem stressors  
    - Cultural heritage impacts  
    - Service delivery disruptions  
    - Carbon storage & productivity decline  
    - Coastal inundation & shoreline erosion  
    - Cryosphere degradation & ground instability  
    - Air quality deterioration  
    - Agricultural pests & diseases  
    - Agricultural system shifts  
    - Potential gains


- Each category has sample keywords + regex rules to ensure consistent matches.  
- Rows with only hazards (no consequences) are dropped.  
- Multiple categories can apply; results stored in `ImpactCategories`.  

```{r,echo=FALSE}

  "(?i)\\b(cultural[- ]?heritage|cultural[- ]?historical values|heritage site(s)?|monument(s)?).*(damage|destroy|degrad|loss)\\b",
  
"Service delivery disruptions",
"water/electricity/sanitation/waste/telecom services disrupted/failing; cold chain affected",
"(?i)\\b(
    service(s)? (disrupt|interruption) |
    water service(s)? (disrupt|interruption) |
    electricit(?:y|y services?) (disrupt|interruption) |
    sanitation (service|system)s? (disrupt|failure) |
    cold chain (storage|facilit(?:y|ies)) (impacted|disrupted) |telecommunications|
    waste management (system|services?) (impacted|disrupted) |energy infrastructure|
    (telecommunication(s)?|broadband|internet|ICT|communication network(s)?) (disrupt|failure)
)\\b",


  "Carbon storage & productivity decline",
  "NPP decline; reduced net primary productivity; soil carbon stocks decline; lower sequestration",
  "(?i)\\b((net primary productivity|NPP) (declin|decreas|reduc)|Net primary productivity|forest productivity|soil carbon stocks? (declin|decreas|reduc)|carbon sequestration (declin|decreas|reduc))\\b",

  "Coastal inundation & shoreline erosion",
  "coastal erosion/retreat; shoreline retreat; permanent inundation; coastal/storm-surge flooding; land loss to sea; tidal/nuisance flooding; below the high tide line",
  "(?i)\\b(coastal (erosion|retreat|inundation|flood(ing)?)|shoreline (retreat|erosion)|beach (erosion|loss)|land loss (to|from) the sea|sea level|Sea-level rise|level of the sea|sea levels|sea level rise|permanent inundation|storm surge (inundation|flood(ing)?)|tidal flooding|nuisance flooding|below the high tide line)\\b",

  "Cryosphere degradation & ground instability",
  "permafrost thaw/degradation; active layer thickening; thermokarst; ground subsidence/instability; frost heave; glacier melt/retreat; reduced snow cover",
  "(?i)\\b(permafrost (thaw|degrad|melt)|active layer (thicken|deepening)|glacier|ice|thermokarst|permafrost|ground (subsidence|instability)|frost heave|glacier (melt|retreat|shrinkage)|snow cover (declin|reduc|loss))\\b",


  "Air quality deterioration",
  "air pollution; poor air quality; PM2.5/PM10; particulate matter; ozone/smog; smoke; haze; dust storms",
  "(?i)\\b(air (pollution|quality (declin|deteriorat|worsen))|PM\\s?(2\\.5|10)\\b|particulate matter|ground[- ]?level ozone|ozone\\b|smog|greenhouse gas emissions|pollution|smoke|haze|dust storm(s)?)\\b",

  "Agricultural pests & diseases",
  "crop pest/disease outbreaks;pest infestations;pests;alien species pathogen pressure; spread of pests; pest incidence; incidence/severity/spread; overwintering pests; higher pesticide use",
  "(?i)\\b((crop|agricultur\\w*) (pest(s)?|disease(s)?|pathogen(s)?)( outbreak(s)?| incidence| incidences| occurrence(s)?| pressure| severity| spread)|overwintering (pests|insects)|invasion|alien species|pest|pests|higher pesticide use|pest|pests|pesticide (use|usage) (increase|rising|higher))\\b",

  "Agricultural system shifts",
  "growing season lengthened/shortened; earlier green-up; delayed senescence; planting boundary shifting northward/poleward/higher elevations;phenology; multi-cropping index rising;shift to higher elevations;shifting in agro-ecological zones;shifting in production zones;frost damage; cropping systems shifting",
  "(?i)\\b(growing season (lengthen(?:ed|ing)?|shorten(?:ed|ing)?)|climate suitability|phenology|geographic distribution|shift to higher elevations|shifting in agro-ecological zones|shift|shifting|shift in production zones|phenological|earlier green[- ]?up|delayed senescence|planting boundary (shift(?:ing)?|moving) (northward|poleward|to higher (latitudes|altitudes|elevations))|multi-?cropping (index|area(s)?) (increase|rising|expanded)|cropping system(s)? (shift|change))\\b",

"Potential gains",
"longer/extended growing season; increased crop yields/productivity/production; increased timber; increased NPP/biomass;attractive; multi-cropping index rising;increase crop yields;positive effect;beneficial;reduce heating demand; new species compositions improving services; reduced heating demand",
"(?i)\\b((longer|extended|lengthen(?:ed|ing))\\s+growing\\s+season(s)?|increase(?:d|s|ing)\\s+(?:crop\\s+)?(?:yield(s)?|productivity|production)\\b(?![^.]{0,20}\\b(decreas|declin|loss|reduct))|increase(?:d|s|ing)\\s+(?:NPP|biomass|forest\\s+productivity|ecosystem\\s+productivity)\\b(?![^.]{0,20}\\b(decreas|declin|loss|reduct))|multi-?cropping\\s+index(es)?\\s+(?:increase|rising|higher)|new\\s+species\\s+composition(s)?\\s+(?:improv(?:e|ing)|enhanc(?:e|ing))\\s+ecosystem\\s+services|reduced\\s+heating\\s+demand|increase\\s+crop\\s+yields?|yield increasing|expand production|positive effects|increase\\s+in\\s+the\\s+performance|increased crop yields|increased\\s+availability\\s+of\\s+feed|expand\\s+the\\s+areas\\s+suitable\\s+for\\s+agriculture|increasing\\s+productivity|reduce heating demand|expansion\\s+of\\s+the\\s+crop\\s+production|increasing\\s+efficiency|facilitating\\s+access|reduction\\s+of\\s+energy\\s+consumption)\\b"
)

# --- Ensure every Keywords phrase is covered by the Regex for its category ---

escape_regex <- function(x) str_replace_all(x, "([\\.^$|?*+()\\[\\]{}])", "\\\\\\1")
hyphen_flexible <- function(x) str_replace_all(x, "\\s*[–-]\\s*", "\\\\s*[–-]\\\\s*")

token_to_pattern <- function(token) {
  token <- str_squish(token)
  if (token == "") return("")
  alts <- str_split(token, "/", simplify = TRUE) %>% as.character()
  alts <- escape_regex(alts) %>% hyphen_flexible()
  if (length(alts) == 1) alts else paste0("(?:", paste(alts, collapse="|"), ")")
}

phrase_to_regex <- function(phrase) {
  tokens <- str_split(str_squish(phrase), "\\s+", simplify = TRUE) %>% as.character()
  if (!length(tokens)) return("")
  pats <- map_chr(tokens, token_to_pattern)
  paste0("\\\\b", paste(pats, collapse="\\\\s+"), "\\\\b")
}

keywords_to_regex <- function(keywords) {
  phrases <- str_split(keywords, ";", simplify = TRUE) %>% as.character() %>% str_trim()
  phrases <- phrases[nzchar(phrases)]
  if (!length(phrases)) return("")
  paste(map_chr(phrases, phrase_to_regex), collapse="|")
}

strip_leading_caseflag <- function(rx) rx %>% str_replace("^\\(\\?i\\)", "") %>% str_squish()

ensure_keywords_covered <- function(tbl) {
  tbl %>%
    mutate(
      .kw_regex = map_chr(Keywords, keywords_to_regex),
      .existing = map_chr(Regex, strip_leading_caseflag),
      Regex = pmap_chr(list(.existing, .kw_regex), function(exist, kw) {
        if (!nzchar(exist) && !nzchar(kw)) return("(?i)")
        if (!nzchar(exist)) return(paste0("(?i)(?:", kw, ")"))
        if (!nzchar(kw))   return(paste0("(?i)", exist))
        paste0("(?i)(?:", exist, "|", kw, ")")
      })
    ) %>%
    select(-.kw_regex, -.existing)
}

impact_categories <- ensure_keywords_covered(impact_categories)

# ---- Matching helpers & pipeline ----

# Read your extracted keywords file
adaptdata <- read_csv("data/adaptdata_climateimpact6nano.csv")

# Sanity check
stopifnot(exists("impact_categories"),
          all(c("Category","Regex","Keywords") %in% names(impact_categories)))

clean_ci_text <- function(x) {
  x %>% str_replace_all("<[^>]+>", " ") %>% str_squish()
}

# Optionally drop rows that only list hazards (no consequences)
hazard_only_regex <- "(?i)\\b(drought(s)?|flood(s|ing)?|storm(s)?|storm surge(s)?|cyclone(s)?|typhoon(s)?|hurricane(s)?|heatwave(s)?|heat wave(s)?|heavy rainfall|rainstorm(s)?|sea[ -]?level rise|landslide(s)?|wildfire(s)?|windstorm(s)?)\\b"

match_categories <- function(txt, map = impact_categories, drop_hazard_only = TRUE) {
  if (is.na(txt) || !nzchar(txt)) return(character(0))
  s <- clean_ci_text(txt)

  if (drop_hazard_only) {
    any_consequence <- any(str_detect(s, map$Regex))
    only_hazard <- (!any_consequence) && str_detect(s, hazard_only_regex)
    if (only_hazard) return(character(0))
  }

  hits <- map$Category[ map_lgl(map$Regex, ~ str_detect(s, .x)) ]
  unique(hits)
}

categorize_ci_vector <- function(v, map = impact_categories, drop_hazard_only = TRUE) {
  map_chr(v, ~{
    cats <- match_categories(.x, map = map, drop_hazard_only = drop_hazard_only)
    if (length(cats) == 0) NA_character_ else paste(cats, collapse = "; ")
  })
}

# ---- Create ONE column with semicolon-separated categories ----
adaptdata <- adaptdata %>%
  mutate(
    ImpactCategories = categorize_ci_vector(ClimateImpact_Keywords,
                                            map = impact_categories,
                                            drop_hazard_only = TRUE)
  )

# Coverage metric (fixed object name)
coverage <- mean(!is.na(adaptdata$ImpactCategories))
message(sprintf("Impact categorization coverage: %.1f %%", 100 * coverage))
```

## 4.3 include the relevant system at risk rows

```{r,echo=FALSE}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr); library(stringr); library(purrr); library(tibble); library(readr); library(rlang)
})

# Preconditions: already defined: impact_categories, clean_ci_text(), categorize_ci_vector(), adaptdata
stopifnot(
  exists("impact_categories"),
  all(c("Category","Regex","Keywords") %in% names(impact_categories)),
  exists("categorize_ci_vector"),
  exists("clean_ci_text"),
  exists("adaptdata")
)

# -- Pull System-at-risk rows (case-insensitive)
sys <- adaptdata %>%
  filter(tolower(Element) == "system at risk")

# -- Keep SAR rows whose ElementLabel suggests impacts/risks or hazards
impactish_rx <- regex(
  "(?i)\\b(impact(s)?|risk(s)?|vulnerab|disaster(s)?|observed impacts?|projected impacts?|impacts?[,\\s]+risks?|risks?[,\\s]+vulnerab|vulnerability (and|&)? impacts?)\\b",
  ignore_case = TRUE
)
hazardish_rx <- regex(
  "(?i)\\b(flood(s|ing)?|drought(s)?|heat( wave(s)?)?|heavy precipitation|precipitation( patterns| projections)?|rain(fall)?|cyclone(s)?|tropical cyclones?|sea level rise|coastal erosion|forest fire(s)?|glacier(|s| retreat(s)?)|desertification|dust( and)? sandstorm(s)?|water scarcity|temperature(s)?|heatwaves?)\\b",
  ignore_case = TRUE
)

sys_filt <- sys %>%
  mutate(.ElementLabel = coalesce(as.character(ElementLabel), "")) %>%
  filter(str_detect(.ElementLabel, impactish_rx) | str_detect(.ElementLabel, hazardish_rx)) %>%
  select(-.ElementLabel)

# -- Build a unified text column to scan (prefer ElementText, then ElementText_MAN)
text_choices <- intersect(c("ElementText", "ElementText_MAN"), names(sys_filt))
if (length(text_choices) == 0L) stop("No ElementText or ElementText_MAN present for System-at-risk rows.")

sys_filt <- sys_filt %>%
  mutate(
    .TextForScan = if (length(text_choices) == 1L)
      .data[[text_choices]]
    else
      coalesce(!!!rlang::syms(text_choices)),
    .TextForScan = na_if(as.character(.TextForScan), ""),
    .TextForScan = clean_ci_text(.TextForScan)
  )

# -- Categorize using your climate-impact regex map (drops hazard-only text internally)
sys_with_impacts <- sys_filt %>%
  mutate(ImpactCategories = categorize_ci_vector(.TextForScan, map = impact_categories, drop_hazard_only = TRUE)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(ImpactCategories)) %>%
  select(-.TextForScan)

# -- If nothing matched, keep original and warn; otherwise clone as Climate impact
if (nrow(sys_with_impacts) == 0L) {
  warning("No System-at-risk rows yielded consequence categories from ElementText; no clones created.")
  adaptdata_augmented <- adaptdata
} else {
  # Ensure these columns exist on base
  if (!"ImpactCategories" %in% names(adaptdata))       adaptdata <- mutate(adaptdata, ImpactCategories = NA_character_)
  if (!"From_SystemAtRisk" %in% names(adaptdata))      adaptdata <- mutate(adaptdata, From_SystemAtRisk = NA)
  if (!"Source_ElementLabel" %in% names(adaptdata))    adaptdata <- mutate(adaptdata, Source_ElementLabel = NA_character_)

  # Clone rows with provenance
  sys_as_ci <- sys_with_impacts %>%
    mutate(
      Element = "Climate impact",
      From_SystemAtRisk = TRUE,
      Source_ElementLabel = as.character(ElementLabel)
    )

  # Column harmonization both ways
  missing_in_clone <- setdiff(names(adaptdata), names(sys_as_ci))
  if (length(missing_in_clone)) {
    sys_as_ci <- bind_cols(sys_as_ci,
      as_tibble(setNames(replicate(length(missing_in_clone), NA, simplify = FALSE), missing_in_clone)))
  }
  missing_in_base <- setdiff(names(sys_as_ci), names(adaptdata))
  if (length(missing_in_base)) {
    adaptdata <- bind_cols(adaptdata,
      as_tibble(setNames(replicate(length(missing_in_base), NA, simplify = FALSE), missing_in_base)))
  }

  # Bind and report
  adaptdata <- bind_rows(adaptdata, sys_as_ci)
}
```

```{r,echo=FALSE}
# ---- Normalizer to merge/fix impact categories ----
normalize_impact_cat <- function(x) {
  lx <- tolower(str_squish(x))

  dplyr::case_when(
    # MERGES
    lx %in% c("human health burden", "mortality & injury", "humna health burden") ~ "Human mortality & morbidity",
    lx %in% c("water quality deterioration", "water availability shortfall")       ~ "Water availability & quality",

    # COMMON TYPOS / CANONICALIZATION
    lx == "economic & livelihood losse"                   ~ "Economic & livelihood losses",
    lx == "livestock imapcts"                             ~ "Livestock impacts",
    lx == "tourism & recreation imapcts"                  ~ "Tourism & recreation impacts",
    lx == "damage to buildings and infrastructure"        ~ "Damage to buildings & infrastructure",
    lx == "energy systems impacts"                        ~ "Energy system impacts",

    # Otherwise keep original (title-ish)
    TRUE ~ str_replace_all(str_to_title(lx),
                           c("\\bAnd\\b"="&",    # small touch to keep your styling
                             " & " = " & "))
  )
}
```

```{r,echo=FALSE}
# Small helper to preview long text with tooltip (keeps your earlier style)
make_preview_html <- function(txt, n = 140) {
  ifelse(
    is.na(txt) | !nzchar(txt), "",
    ifelse(
      nchar(txt) > n,
      paste0("<span title='", txt, "'>", substr(txt, 1, n), "...</span>"),
      txt
    )
  )
}

set.seed(123)  # set for reproducibility; change or remove if you want fresh samples each run

ci_base <- adaptdata %>%
  filter(grepl("^\\s*climate impact\\s*$", Element, ignore.case = TRUE),
         !is.na(ImpactCategories), str_detect(ImpactCategories, "\\S")) %>%
  mutate(
    ElementText_Preview = make_preview_html(ElementText),
    AllCategories = ImpactCategories           # keep the full categories list before we unnest
  )

# Unnest to one row per (row x category), then sample up to 10 per category
sampled_by_cat <- ci_base %>%
  separate_rows(ImpactCategories, sep = ";") %>%
  mutate(ImpactCategories = str_squish(ImpactCategories)) %>%
  filter(ImpactCategories != "") %>%
  group_by(ImpactCategories) %>%
  slice_sample(prop = 1) %>%              # shuffle within each group
  slice_head(n = 10) %>%                  # take first 10 (or fewer)
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(ImpactCategories)

# Build the DT

    transmute(

      `All Selected Categories` = AllCategories
    ),

  options = list(pageLength = 10, autoWidth = TRUE, dom = "tip")
)
```

# Step 5 : Action level and type

## 5.1 Action type

**Goal.** Tag each *Action* with a single **type** to describe the primary adaptation approach.

# Action Type & Intervention Categories

This dataset classifies climate adaptation measures into broad **intervention categories**.  
Each intervention contains **types**, which group related actions, and each type includes specific **actions** (and sometimes subactions).  

## Intervention Categories

### *Ecosystem based*
Focus on maintaining and restoring natural systems.  
Includes intervention types such as:  
- **Biodiversity development** – actions to enhance biodiversity (e.g., ecological buffer zones, pollination support).  
- **Ecological restoration** – restoring degraded ecosystems (e.g., afforestation, climate-resilient trees).  
- **Green infrastructure** – using vegetation and permeable systems for adaptation (e.g., rain gardens, green roofs).  
- **Agroforestry** – integrating trees into agricultural systems.  
- **Animals** – livestock and aquaculture resilience.  
- **Crop diversification** – multiple crops to reduce risk.  
- **Energy** – biogas, improved cookstoves, etc.  
- **Migration** – relocating crops/livestock in response to climate.  
- **Nutrient management** – compost, manure, fertility practices.  
- **Pest and disease management** – integrated pest management, biological control.  
- **Postharvest** – storage, drying, reducing food loss.  
- **Schedule modification** – shifting planting/harvest calendars.  
- **Soil management** – mulching, conservation tillage, improved fallows.  
- **Water management** – irrigation efficiency, water harvesting.

---

### *Institutional*
Policies, governance, and frameworks enabling adaptation.  
Includes:  
- **Economic (policy level)** – finance and incentives from institutions (grants, subsidies, PES).  
- **Government policies and programs** – national/local adaptation plans, sectoral programs.  
- **Laws and regulations** – binding rules such as zoning, building codes, protected areas.  
- **Research development** – climate modeling, monitoring, R&D, policy analysis.

---

### *Social*
Adaptation driven by people, communities, and knowledge.  
Includes:  
- **Behavioural** – household/community practices (diet change, water storage, advocacy).  
- **Educational** – awareness, training, gender & inclusion, extension services.  
- **Informational** – climate/market/health information, early warning systems.  
- **Economic (household level)** – income diversification, livelihood strategies.

---

### *Infrastructure / Structural / Physical*
Hard measures, services, and technology.  
Includes:  
- **Engineered and built environment** – seawalls, dams, drainage, resilient transport.  
- **Services** – service delivery platforms like social protection, healthcare.  
- **Supply-chain improvement** – logistics, storage, market access.  
- **Technological** – precision agriculture, IoT, improved breeds/varieties, renewable energy.




**Method**

- GPT reads the *Action* text and must return **exactly one** of the five labels (or `NA` if unclear).
- The output is saved in `ActionType_GPT` and previewed in a datatable.

```{r,echo=FALSE}
adaptdata<-read.csv("adaptadata_action_type_nano6.csv")

# ---- Quick check --

# ---- Canonical Action Type Mapping ----
intervention_to_action_type <- function(x) {
  raw <- tolower(trimws(x))

  if (raw %in% c("biodiversity development",
                 "ecological restoration",
                 "green infrastructure",
                 "agroforestry",
                 "animals",
                 "crop diversification",
                 "energy",
                 "migration",
                 "nutrient management",
                 "pest and disease management",
                 "postharvest",
                 "schedule modification",
                 "soil management",
                 "water management")) {
    return("ecosystem based")
  }

  if (raw %in% c("economic",
                 "government policies and programs",
                 "laws and regulations",
                 "research development")) {
    return("institutional")
  }

  if (raw %in% c("behavioural",
                 "educational",
                 "informational",
                 "social",
                 "livelihood diversification")) {
    return("social")
  }

  if (raw %in% c("engineered and built environment",
                 "services",
                 "supply-chain improvement",
                 "technological",
                 "renewable energy")) {
    return("infrastructure/structural / physical")
  }

  if (raw %in% c("uncategorized")) {
    return("uncategorized")
  }

  return(NA_character_)
}

# ---- Apply to your classified data ----
if (!"ActionType_GPT" %in% names(adaptdata)) {
  adaptdata$ActionType_GPT <- NA_character_
}

adaptdata$ActionType_GPT <- vapply(adaptdata$InterventionType_GPT,
                                   intervention_to_action_type,
                                   character(1))

```


```{r,echo=FALSE}
.norm_tok <- function(x) {
  x %>% str_replace_all("\\p{Zs}+", " ") %>% str_squish()
}
# B) ACTION TYPE SUMMARY
# ----------------------
type_counts <- adaptdata %>%
  filter(grepl("^\\s*action\\s*$", Element, ignore.case = TRUE),
         !is.na(InterventionType_GPT),
         str_detect(InterventionType_GPT, "\\S")) %>%
  separate_rows(InterventionType_GPT, sep = ";") %>%        # robust if multiple
  mutate(InterventionType_GPT = .norm_tok(InterventionType_GPT)) %>%
  filter(InterventionType_GPT != "") %>%
  count(InterventionType_GPT, sort = TRUE) %>%
  rename(`Action Type` = InterventionType_GPT,
         Occurrences = n)

DT::datatable(
  type_counts,
  rownames = FALSE,
  options = list(pageLength = 10, autoWidth = TRUE, dom = 'tip'),
  caption = "🏷️ Action Type — counts"
)

write.csv(type_counts, "action_type_counts.csv", row.names = FALSE)

type_plot <- ggplot(type_counts,
  aes(x = reorder(`Action Type`, Occurrences),
      y = Occurrences,
      fill = `Action Type`)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "mako") +
  labs(title = "Action Type by count", x = NULL, y = "Occurrences") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14))

type_plot

```

## 5.2 Action level

Action Level classification

**Goal.** Distinguish whether each *Action* reported is **preparatory groundwork** or a **substantive adaptation measure**.

**Definitions**

- **Groundwork** — upstream or enabling work such as:
  - impact/vulnerability assessments, scenarios, conceptual tools  
  - policy recommendations, planning frameworks  
- **Substantive action** — concrete measures such as:
  - organizational development, regulations, awareness/outreach, education/training  
  - monitoring/MEL, infrastructure, technology/innovation  
  - financial mechanisms, resource transfer, funding  

**Method**

- GPT reads each *Action* text and must return **exactly one label**: *Groundwork* or *Substantive action*.  
- If no clear match, the model returns `NA`.  
- The result is stored in `ActionLevel_GPT` and previewed in a datatable.  


```{r,echo=FALSE}
adaptdata<-read.csv("data/adaptdata_action_level_nano6.csv")


# ---- Fix: set missing InterventionType_GPT to "economic" if Element == "Action" ----
adaptdata$InterventionType_GPT <- ifelse(
  is.na(adaptdata$InterventionType_GPT) & 
    grepl("^\\s*action\\s*$", adaptdata$Element, ignore.case = TRUE),
  "economic",
  adaptdata$InterventionType_GPT
)

# --- Action Level & Type summaries (counts + DT + plots) --------------------
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr); library(stringr); library(tidyr)
  library(DT); library(ggplot2); library(readr)
})

# If the current environment doesn't have both columns, try reloading the latest CSV
if (!exists("adaptdata") || !all(c("ActionLevel_GPT","ActionType_GPT") %in% names(adaptdata))) {
  if (file.exists("adaptdata_action_type.csv")) {
    adaptdata <- readr::read_csv("adaptdata_action_type.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
  } else if (file.exists("adaptdata_action_level.csv")) {
    adaptdata <- readr::read_csv("adaptdata_action_level.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
  } else {
    stop("adaptdata with ActionLevel_GPT / ActionType_GPT not found. Run steps 5.1–5.2 first.")
  }
}

# Helper to normalize unicode spaces and trim tokens


# -----------------------
# A) ACTION LEVEL SUMMARY
# -----------------------
level_counts <- adaptdata %>%
  filter(grepl("^\\s*action\\s*$", Element, ignore.case = TRUE),
         !is.na(ActionLevel_GPT),
         str_detect(ActionLevel_GPT, "\\S")) %>%
  count(ActionLevel_GPT, sort = TRUE) %>%
  rename(`Action Level` = ActionLevel_GPT,
         Occurrences = n)


DT::datatable(
  level_counts,
  rownames = FALSE,
  options = list(pageLength = 10, autoWidth = TRUE, dom = 'tip'),
  caption = "🧭 Action Level (Groundwork vs Substantive) — counts"
)


level_props <- level_counts %>%
  mutate(
    Percent = Occurrences / sum(Occurrences),
    midlab  = cumsum(Percent) - Percent/2,
    label   = paste0(round(Percent*100), "%")
  )

# ---- Donut chart ----
donut <- ggplot(level_props, aes(x = 2, y = Occurrences, fill = `Action Level`)) +
  geom_col(width = 1, color = NA) +
  # inner white circle to make the "hole"
  geom_col(data = data.frame(Occurrences = sum(level_props$Occurrences)),
           aes(x = 1, y = Occurrences),
           inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "white", width = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(x = 2, y = cumsum(Occurrences) - Occurrences/2,
                label = label), color = "white", size = 5) +
  coord_polar(theta = "y") +
  xlim(0.5, 2.5) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "viridis") +
  labs(title = "Action level — composition") +
  theme_void(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.title = element_blank())
```

```{r,echo=FALSE}
# --- Bring Region onto adaptdata ---

  select(Country, Region) %>%
  distinct()

# add manual fixes for missing countries
manual_add <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Country,        ~Region,
  "Moldova",       "Eastern Europe",
  "Phillipines",   "Asia-Pacific",
  "Russia",        "Eastern Europe",
  "Türkiye",       "Asia-Pacific",
  "USA",           "Western Europe and Other states"
)

# combine with existing region_key
region_key <- region_key %>%
  bind_rows(manual_add) %>%
  distinct()


adaptdata_with_region <- adaptdata %>%
  dplyr::left_join(region_key, by = "Country") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Region = dplyr::coalesce(Region, "Unknown"))

# --- Counts by Region x Action Level ---
level_counts_region <- adaptdata_with_region %>%
  dplyr::filter(grepl("^\\s*action\\s*$", Element, ignore.case = TRUE),
                !is.na(ActionLevel_GPT),
                stringr::str_detect(ActionLevel_GPT, "\\S")) %>%
  dplyr::count(Region, ActionLevel_GPT, name = "Occurrences") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ActionLevel_GPT = factor(ActionLevel_GPT, 
                                         levels = c("Groundwork","Substantive action")))

# --- Stacked bars: one bar per Region; colors = Action Level (counts) ---

  level_counts_region,

      y = Occurrences,
      fill = ActionLevel_GPT)
) +
  geom_col(position = "stack") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "plasma", name = "Action Level") +
  labs(title = "Action level by UNFCCC region (stacked counts)",
       x = NULL, y = "Occurrences") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +

level_plot_region_counts
```

```{r,echo=FALSE}
make_preview_html <- function(txt, n = 140) {
  ifelse(
    is.na(txt) | !nzchar(txt), "",
    ifelse(
      nchar(txt) > n,
      paste0("<span title='", txt, "'>", substr(txt, 1, n), "...</span>"),
      txt
    )
  )
}

  )
```

# Step 6 : Results

**Goal.** Label each *Result* as one of four types so we can compare what’s being reported across countries and sectors.

**Method**  
- GPT reads the *Result* text and returns **exactly one label** from the list above (or `NA` if unclear).  
- We **store the model’s reply verbatim** in `ResultType_GPT` (no normalization here); any cleanup or remapping happens later.

```{r,echo=FALSE,}
# DEFINITIONS (updated; strict ranking Impact > Outcome > Output)

# - Impact — Ultimate effects relative to climate risks (adequacy/effectiveness) OR improved system condition/vulnerability, even without numbers:
#   • reduced risk/impacts/harm (fewer deaths/injuries/damages/losses; avoided losses); faster/better hazard response/recovery;
#   • resilience/adaptive capacity strengthened or vulnerability reduced;

#   • agricultural productivity/yields ↑ or losses ↓;

# - Outcome — Intermediate CHANGES in behavior or condition (not the ultimate effect):
#   • adoption/use/operation increased; access/coverage/connection/participation/share/rate increased (change from baseline);
#   • integration/coordination/practices established and running (e.g., routine reporting, monitoring systems operating);
#   • service reliability/preparedness/capacity improved, where hazard adequacy/effect is not claimed.

#   • finance mobilized/allocated/spent; risk analyses/maps/datasets/baselines/assessments/guidelines produced.
```

```{r,echo=FALSE,}
# --- Results: simple bar chart (Input / Process / Output / Outcome) ---
adaptdata<-read.csv("data/adaptdata_results_nano6.csv")

RESULT_LABELS <- c("Output","Outcome","Impact")



result_counts <- adaptdata %>%
  filter(Element == "Result",
         !is.na(ResultType_GPT),
         nzchar(ResultType_GPT)) %>%
  mutate(ResultType_GPT = str_squish(ResultType_GPT)) %>%
  # map to canonical labels & drop anything off-list (just in case)
  mutate(ResultType_GPT = sapply(ResultType_GPT, function(t) {
    hit <- RESULT_LABELS[tolower(RESULT_LABELS) == tolower(t)]
    ifelse(length(hit), hit, NA_character_)
  })) %>%
  filter(!is.na(ResultType_GPT)) %>%
  mutate(ResultType_GPT = factor(ResultType_GPT, levels = RESULT_LABELS)) %>%
  count(ResultType_GPT, name = "Occurrences") %>%
  arrange(ResultType_GPT) %>%
  mutate(Share = Occurrences / sum(Occurrences),
         Label = paste0(Occurrences, " (", round(Share*100), "%)"))


# horizontal bars with counts + %
p_results <- ggplot(result_counts,
  aes(x = ResultType_GPT, y = Occurrences, fill = ResultType_GPT)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = Label), hjust = -0.15, size = 4) +
  coord_flip(ylim = c(0, max(result_counts$Occurrences)*1.15)) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +  # swap palette if you like
  labs(title = "Result types by count",
       x = NULL, y = "Occurrences") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 13),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12))

p_results

#####Results using manual tagging 
result_counts_manual <- adaptdata %>%
  filter(Element == "Result",
         !is.na(ResultType),
         nzchar(ResultType)) %>%
  mutate(ResultType = str_squish(ResultType)) %>%
  # keep only canonical labels and order them
  mutate(ResultType = sapply(ResultType, function(t) {
    hit <- RESULT_LABELS[tolower(RESULT_LABELS) == tolower(t)]
    ifelse(length(hit), hit, NA_character_)
  })) %>%
  filter(!is.na(ResultType)) %>%
  mutate(ResultType = factor(ResultType, levels = RESULT_LABELS)) %>%
  count(ResultType, name = "Occurrences") %>%
  arrange(ResultType) %>%
  mutate(Share = Occurrences / sum(Occurrences),
         Label = paste0(Occurrences, " (", round(Share*100), "%)"))

# Plot
p_results_manual <- ggplot(result_counts_manual,
  aes(x = ResultType, y = Occurrences, fill = ResultType)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = Label), hjust = -0.15, size = 4) +
  coord_flip(ylim = c(0, max(result_counts$Occurrences)*1.15)) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  labs(title = "Result types by count",
       x = NULL, y = "Occurrences") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 13),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12))
```

# Step 7 : Adaptation priorities

List of adaptation priorities : 
- **Water use efficiency & demand management** — Reduce water losses and improve irrigation efficiency/productivity.  
- **Alternative & non-conventional water resources** — Options like rainwater harvesting, greywater reuse, desalination, and storage.  
- **Agribusiness enhancement & private sector development** — Strengthening agribusinesses, value chains, and SME/market linkages.  
- **Legal, policy & institutional frameworks** — Laws, policies, governance, and institutional capacity for adaptation.  
- **Climate-smart agriculture (CSA) & resilient farming systems** — Practices like crop diversification, agroforestry, and soil management.  
- **Sustainable land & farm management** — Sustainable land practices, organic/landscape approaches.  
- **Climate-resilient crops & seeds** — Breeding and access to drought/heat/pest-resistant varieties and seeds.  
- **Farmer capacity, extension & knowledge services** — Training, extension services, and farmer knowledge exchange.  
- **Agricultural water management** — On-farm water efficiency, watershed management, and irrigation.  
- **Rural development & livelihood diversification** — Enhancing rural infrastructure, markets, and income sources.  
- **Ecosystem protection, restoration & protected areas** — Conserving and restoring ecosystems and biodiversity.  
- **Combat land degradation & desertification** — Tackling soil erosion, fertility loss, and desertification.  
- **Afforestation, reforestation & carbon sinks** — Tree planting and forest cover expansion for carbon sequestration.  
- **Invasive species management** — Control and management of invasive alien species.  
- **Land-use & spatial planning integration** — Adaptation in zoning, territorial, and land-use planning.  
- **Monitoring, data & hydrological observation** — Climate monitoring, data systems, and hydrological observation.  
- **National adaptation frameworks & strategies** — National-level plans/frameworks (e.g., NAP, NCCAS).  
- **Local adaptation capacity & community empowerment** — Community-based adaptation and local empowerment.  
- **Public awareness, education & engagement** — Campaigns, curricula, and awareness programs.  
- **Institutional & technical capacity building** — Training, institutional strengthening, inter-agency coordination.  
- **Policy mainstreaming & regulatory integration** — Integrating adaptation into policies and regulations.  
- **Cross-sectoral collaboration & partnerships** — Partnerships and coordination across sectors.  
- **Data management, knowledge & information services** — Knowledge management, sharing, and tools.  
- **Evidence base, risk & impact assessments** — Vulnerability, risk, and impact assessments.  
- **Subnational adaptation priorities & sector packages** — Region- or sector-specific strategies and action packages.  
- **Agro-meteorological & climate information services** — Forecasts, advisories, and information services for agriculture.  
- **Post-harvest, food loss reduction & risk transfer** — Reducing losses, value addition, insurance, and cold chains.  
- **Climate-resilient livestock systems** — Livestock management, resilient breeds, and animal health.  
- **Research, innovation & investment (agri/health)** — Research, technology, and innovation in agriculture and health.  
- **Fire management & response capability** — Fire prevention, management, and emergency response.  
- **Community-based forest management & re/afforestation** — Local forest management and reforestation.  
- **Biodiversity assessment & monitoring** — Biodiversity inventories, monitoring, and assessments.  
- **Public health: surveillance, systems & workforce** — Disease surveillance, early warning, and health workforce.  
- **Public health infrastructure & services** — Facilities, WASH, energy, and resilient health services.  
- **Urban climate resilience & planning** — Climate-proofed urban planning and infrastructure.  
- **Urban green/blue infrastructure & heat mitigation** — Greening, cooling, water-sensitive infrastructure.  
- **Disaster risk reduction, EWS & emergency management** — DRR, early warning systems, and emergency response.  
- **Energy & grid resilience** — Strengthening energy infrastructure and supply chains.  
- **Coastal & marine ecosystem protection/restoration** — Mangroves, reefs, wetlands, and coastal restoration.  
- **Agricultural resource efficiency & high-standard farmland** — Efficient farmland, fertilizer, and input use.  
- **Water allocation, security & quantified targets** — Ensuring water security with defined consumption/coverage targets.  
- **Transport infrastructure & services adaptation** — Climate-proofing roads, ports, rail, and mobility.  
- **Industry & mining adaptation** — Industrial resilience and climate-compatible mining.  
- **Sectoral adaptation plans & guidelines** — Guidelines and action plans for specific sectors (e.g., tourism).  
- **Finance, insurance & social protection** — Climate finance, insurance, and social safety nets.  
- **Tourism sector adaptation** — Adaptation strategies for tourism and ecotourism.  
- **Gender & social inclusion** — Gender-sensitive and socially inclusive adaptation approaches.

```{r,echo=FALSE}
adaptdata<-read.csv("adaptdata_results_nano6.csv")

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr); library(stringr); library(purrr); library(tibble); library(readr); library(rlang)
})

# -----------------------------
# Helper functions (same style as your impact classifier)
# -----------------------------
escape_regex <- function(x) str_replace_all(x, "([\\.^$|?*+()\\[\\]{}])", "\\\\\\1")
hyphen_flexible <- function(x) str_replace_all(x, "\\s*[–-]\\s*", "\\\\s*[–-]\\\\s*")

token_to_pattern <- function(token) {
  token <- str_squish(token)
  if (token == "") return("")
  alts <- str_split(token, "/", simplify = TRUE) %>% as.character()
  alts <- escape_regex(alts) %>% hyphen_flexible()
  if (length(alts) == 1) alts else paste0("(?:", paste(alts, collapse="|"), ")")
}

phrase_to_regex <- function(phrase) {
  tokens <- str_split(str_squish(phrase), "\\s+", simplify = TRUE) %>% as.character()
  if (!length(tokens)) return("")
  pats <- map_chr(tokens, token_to_pattern)
  paste0("\\\\b", paste(pats, collapse="\\\\s+"), "\\\\b")
}

keywords_to_regex <- function(keywords) {
  phrases <- str_split(keywords, ";", simplify = TRUE) %>% as.character() %>% str_trim()
  phrases <- phrases[nzchar(phrases)]
  if (!length(phrases)) return("")
  paste(map_chr(phrases, phrase_to_regex), collapse="|")
}

strip_leading_caseflag <- function(rx) rx %>% str_replace("^\\(\\?i\\)", "") %>% str_squish()

ensure_keywords_covered <- function(tbl) {
  tbl %>%
    mutate(
      .kw_regex = map_chr(Keywords, keywords_to_regex),
      .existing = map_chr(Regex, strip_leading_caseflag),
      Regex = pmap_chr(list(.existing, .kw_regex), function(exist, kw) {
        if (!nzchar(exist) && !nzchar(kw)) return("(?i)")
        if (!nzchar(exist)) return(paste0("(?i)(?:", kw, ")"))
        if (!nzchar(kw))   return(paste0("(?i)", exist))
        paste0("(?i)(?:", exist, "|", kw, ")")
      })
    ) %>%
    select(-.kw_regex, -.existing)
}

clean_ap_text <- function(x) x %>% str_replace_all("<[^>]+>", " ") %>% str_squish()

  "Water allocation, security & quantified targets",
  "water security; total water consumption; consumption cap; optimized allocation of water resources; water supply capacity; emergency backup water sources; rural tap water coverage; national water security",
  "(?i)\\b(water\\s+security|total\\s+water\\s+consumption|consumption\\s+cap|optim(?:i|)s(?:e|ed)\\s+allocation\\s+of\\s+water\\s+resources|water\\s+supply\\s+capacity|emergency\\s+backup\\s+water\\s+source(?:s)?|rural\\s+tap\\s+water\\s+coverage|national\\s+water\\s+security)\\b",

  "Transport infrastructure & services adaptation",
  "improved transport infrastructure and services; roads; railways; ports; airports; mobility",
  "(?i)\\b(transport\\s+(?:infrastructure|services)|roads?|railways?|ports?|airports?|mobility|transport)\\b",

  "Industry & mining adaptation",
  "climate compatible mining; industrial adaptation; industry resilience",
  "(?i)\\b(mining|climate\\s+compatible\\s+mining|industrial\\s+adaptation|industry\\s+resilience)\\b",

  "Sectoral adaptation plans & guidelines",
  "sector adaptation plans; sector guidelines; sector risk assessments; sector action plans; tourism guidelines; action plans for the sector",
  "(?i)\\b(sector(?:al)?\\s+(?:adaptation\\s+)?plans?|sector\\s+guidelines?|sector\\s+risk\\s+assessments?|sector\\s+action\\s+plans?|tourism\\s+guidelines?)\\b",

  "Finance, insurance & social protection",
  "mobilize capital; mobilizing capital; mobilization of capital; green investments; access to climate finance; insurance; social safety nets; capital markets; credit lines; enterprise funds; CCCF",
  "(?i)\\b(mobiliz(?:e|ing|ation)\\s+(?:capital|investment)|green\\s+investments?|access\\s+to\\s+climate\\s+finance|insurance|social\\s+safety\\s+nets?|capital\\s+markets?|credit\\s+lines?|enterprise\\s+funds?|\\bCCCFs?|funds|funding\\b)\\b",

  "Tourism sector adaptation",
  "tourism sector; seaside tourism; tourism model; ecotourism; tourism action plans",
  "(?i)\\b(tourism|seaside\\s+tourism|tourism\\s+model|ecotourism|tourism\\s+action\\s+plans?)\\b",

  "Gender & social inclusion",
  "gender perspective; women; girls; indigenous people; just transition; inclusion; vulnerable groups",
  "(?i)\\b(gender\\s+perspective|women|girls|indigenous|just\\s+transition|inclusion|vulnerable\\s+groups|just transition|aboriginal)\\b"
)

# Merge manual Regex with auto-generated one from Keywords
priority_categories <- ensure_keywords_covered(priority_categories)

# -----------------------------
# Classifier
# -----------------------------
match_priorities <- function(txt, map = priority_categories) {
  if (is.na(txt) || !nzchar(txt)) return(character(0))
  s <- clean_ap_text(txt)
  hits <- map$Category[ map_lgl(map$Regex, ~ str_detect(s, .x)) ]
  unique(hits)
}

categorize_priority_vector <- function(v, map = priority_categories) {
  map_chr(v, ~{
    cats <- match_priorities(.x, map = map)
    if (length(cats) == 0) NA_character_ else paste(cats, collapse = "; ")
  })
}

# -----------------------------
# Apply to your data (Element == "Adaptation priorities")
# -----------------------------
stopifnot(exists("adaptdata"))

# Select the text column (prefer ElementText, fallback ElementText_MAN, else NA)
text_choices <- intersect(c("ElementText", "ElementText_MAN"), names(adaptdata))
if (length(text_choices) == 0L) stop("No ElementText or ElementText_MAN columns found.")

ap_rows <- adaptdata %>% filter(tolower(Element) == "adaptation priorities")

if (nrow(ap_rows) > 0) {
  ap_rows <- ap_rows %>%
    mutate(.TextForScan = coalesce(!!!rlang::syms(text_choices))) %>%
    mutate(PriorityCategories = categorize_priority_vector(.TextForScan)) %>%
    select(-.TextForScan)

  # Ensure column exists on base; then left-join updates back (keeps original row order)
  # Ensure column exists in adaptdata
if (!"PriorityCategories" %in% names(adaptdata)) {
  adaptdata <- adaptdata %>% mutate(PriorityCategories = NA_character_)
}

# Update only rows that are adaptation priorities
adaptdata <- adaptdata %>%
  mutate(
    PriorityCategories = if_else(
      tolower(Element) == "adaptation priorities",
      categorize_priority_vector(coalesce(!!!rlang::syms(text_choices))),
      PriorityCategories
    )
  )


  cov_ap <- adaptdata %>%
    filter(tolower(Element) == "adaptation priorities") %>%
    summarise(cov = mean(!is.na(PriorityCategories))) %>% pull(cov)

  message(sprintf("Adaptation priorities categorization coverage: %.1f%%",
                  100 * cov_ap))
} else {
  message("No rows with Element == 'Adaptation priorities' found.")
}

# Optional export:
# write_csv(adaptdata, "adaptdata_with_priority_categories_nano6.csv")


```



by regions

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(DT)


region_key <- overview %>%
  select(Country, Region) %>%
  distinct()

# add manual fixes for missing countries
manual_add <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Country,        ~Region,
  "Moldova",       "Eastern Europe",
  "Phillipines",   "Asia-Pacific",
  "Russia",        "Eastern Europe",
  "Türkiye",       "Asia-Pacific",
  "USA",           "Western Europe and Other states"
)

# combine with existing region_key
region_key <- region_key %>%
  bind_rows(manual_add) %>%
  distinct()


adaptdata_with_region <- adaptdata %>%
  left_join(region_key, by = "Country")

# 1) Counts by Region x Priority
priority_counts_region <- adaptdata_with_region %>%
  filter(tolower(Element) == "adaptation priorities",
         !is.na(PriorityCategories),
         str_detect(PriorityCategories, "\\S")) %>%
  separate_rows(PriorityCategories, sep = ";") %>%
  mutate(
    PriorityCategories = str_squish(PriorityCategories),
    Region = if_else(is.na(Region) | !nzchar(Region), "Unknown", Region)
  ) %>%
  filter(PriorityCategories != "") %>%
  count(Region, PriorityCategories, sort = TRUE) %>%
  rename(`Priority Category` = PriorityCategories,
         Occurrences = n)

# 2) Pick TOP 20 categories by total across regions
top20 <- priority_counts_region %>%
  group_by(`Priority Category`) %>%
  summarise(Total = sum(Occurrences), .groups = "drop") %>%
  slice_max(Total, n = 20, with_ties = FALSE)

priority_counts_region_top20 <- priority_counts_region %>%
  semi_join(top20, by = "Priority Category") %>%
  left_join(top20, by = "Priority Category") %>%
  mutate(`Priority Category` = reorder(`Priority Category`, Total)) %>%
  arrange(Total)

# 3) Stacked plot by Region (top 20 only)
priority_plot_region <- ggplot(priority_counts_region_top20,
  aes(x = `Priority Category`, y = Occurrences, fill = Region)) +
  geom_col(position = "stack") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "plasma", name = "Region") +
  labs(title = "Top 20 adaptation priorities by UNFCCC region (stacked)",
       x = NULL, y = "Occurrences") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10)

priority_plot_region
```

```{r,echo=FALSE}
library(tidyr)

priority_table_region <- priority_counts_region %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Region,
    values_from = Occurrences,
    values_fill = 0
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(rowSums(across(where(is.numeric)))))

DT::datatable(

  options = list(
    pageLength = 15,
    autoWidth = TRUE,

)
```
